applies_why: The judge text decides whether Jeremiah 22:30 has any live link to contradict after C4 pressed it, so it falls under the rule governing counting a verse as an unanswered witness.
quote: C4 pressed against the curse limb the defender dropped in [CR3] LINK 5, so no live link remains to contradict; the dropping is recorded there.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: Interpreted 'counts as an unanswered witness': either the judge is counting Jeremiah 22:30 as an unanswered witness by noting C4 pressed it against the dropped curse limb, or the judge is only recording that the pressed limb was dropped so no live link remains and is not counting the verse.
why: The judge does not count Jeremiah 22:30 as an unanswered witness; it treats the pressed limb as dropped and says no live link remains to contradict, which is not counting and therefore obeys the rule.
